recipes.name: Garlic Lemon Mahi Filets
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.
Stir wine, lemon juice, garlic, salt, and black pepper together in a shallow bowl. Place mahi mahi fillets in the bowl and turn to coat; allow to marinate for 10 minutes.
Remove fillets from marinade, shaking off any excess moisture. Discard marinade.
Cook fillets on the preheated grill until fish flakes easily with a fork, 4 to 5 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Lemon Mahi Filets
raw_recipe.description: This mahi mahi with a marinade of lemon juice, white Zinfandel wine, and garlic gives fish fillets a nice flavor before cooking over a hot grill.

review.reviewBody: I cut the recipe in half and cooked it in the oven at 350 for 20 minutes. I didn't marinate it, I just threw all the ingredients in the casserole dish (I lessened the wine a little for this reason). Next time I will add tomatoes and green onions. This is a great base recipe and it's easy to throw together with ingredients you have on hand. It can be used on any fish, not just Mahi Mahi, even shrimp. I also did not find it bland as other people did. Thanks for the recipe.

Extremely flavorful!! My first time cooking Mahi Mahi and it will not be my last. This had to be the best gourmet dish I have ever made. My 24 year old daughter said how she could taste the garlic and it was not overpowering. I did cook the fish in a skillet with olive oil and the fish had an awesome caramelization on both sides. I served it with fresh green beans that were boiled for about 5 minutes. 4 tbsp. butter in skillet and saute pecans. Add green beans and 4 tsp. zest of lemon and some fresh italian parsley. It was awesome!! You will definitely not be disappointed with this recipe and it doesn't take a lot of time either. Bon Appetit.

I made only one change, I didn’t have White Zinfandel, so I used a high quality Pinot Grigio. Cooked it on the grill, I should have reduced the time since my pieces of fish were small. Great results, definitely a keeper.

VERY quick, easy, and delicious! I cooked this in a pan, on medium heat, with two tablespoons of sesame oil. (I kept all other ingredients the same.) The fish caramelized beautifully on both sides and the flavor was fantastic. Only substitution I recommend: FRESH-ground black pepper (12 turns directly into the marinade from a pepper mill). I will be making this again and again -- one of the best fish dishes I've ever had.

Grilled a full side of mahi-mahi on the grill, and it came out perfect!! I added a lilikoi in the marinade and grilled it topped with slices of lilikoi and lemon and glazed it with lemon juice as it was grilling. It came out moist and flavorful. Simple and fresh recipe!

Adding this to my recipe book...it’s quick, easy, healthy, and moist with a wonderfully light flavor! I baked the dish in the marinade at 350 degrees for 20 minutes (10 minutes each side). And I served it along side steamed asparagus with hollandaise sauce and steamed cauliflower. My family loved it!

This was a great recipe. A nice light and tasteful marinade for fish. I did not use lemon juice. Since I was using fresh garlic I used the lemon zest of a large lemon and it turned out fantastic. I also added some grape tomatoes and baked it in the oven.

It’s a very light flavor and I think I’ll give it at least a couple hours to marinate next time. But my son that hates fish devoured it so I’m keeping it on the menu even though I would’ve liked more flavor.

This turned out very well with me using a sweet white wine since that is all I had. I sprinkled each filet with salt and pepper instead of measuring it out, and I baked it in the oven with the marinade --about 20 minutes at 400. The fish had a very nice flavor.
Added a pinch of Old Bay & EVOO to my marinade, cooked about 6mins per side, turned out awesome! My daughter killed it! Great recipe!

Great marinade for mahi-mahi. I used chardonnay and it worked just fine. For the "not enough flavor" comment, you want a subtle marinade for a lighter fish like mahi-mahi. Most fish marinades beat you over the head with the flavors, whereas this one delicately compliments the fish nicely. A nice caper butter can help for those needing more kick.
Sorry to give such a low rating. I love grilling fish. Usually salmon or mahi. This was just bland. I know mahi's flavor is mild, so the marinade needed a bit more flavor.

There is not overwhelming the flavor of the fish and there is not adding any flavor to the fish. This recipe fell into the latter category. It was just too bland. You could kind of taste the lemon. 

I would not make again.
I will definitely make it again. The zest is what makes it. Fresh, light and very flavorful.
Fish was very moist. Just needed a little something extra (reason for 4 stars). Next time, adding some lemon pepper seasoning.
Terribly bland
Great recipe. We really enjoyed it.
Made it exactly as described during and enjoyed it immensely
I only rated two stars, because maybe I need to marinate it longer or something. Because it came out dry. But, I will try again. Thanks
The fish had no flavor. Tasteless.
